clue.text: Spooks surrounding base after revolution that's bloodless

indicators.note: after revolution says the whole assembled piece is then turned round to read backwards
surrounding says the spies' letters go round the word for base

parts.note: spooks are spies, and the CIA is the American spy agency
base in the sense of low or ignoble means mean

explanation.surface: Ghosts gather round a pale, drained figure who has just come through an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising, but it means a turn: the wrapped piece is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a shortage of red blood cells, so an anaemic person looks pale and drained, as if without blood.

clue.text: Items up for discussion: time and bucks

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: bucks means jerks about wildly, like a horse, so the letters of and are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A meeting's list of topics: how long it takes and how many dollars it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' looks like dollars, but it is a verb telling us to jumble AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of business to be dealt with at a meeting, the points to be debated.

clue.text: African after injury refuses foot ointment?

indicators.note: after injury says the remaining letters are hurt and come out rearranged
refuses means the foot's letter is turned away and dropped

explanation.surface: A wounded African turns down a balm for his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuses' removes F from AFRICAN, leaving ARICAN; 'after injury' jumbles those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnica is a herbal remedy, often used as a cream or gel on bruises; the question mark admits it is only sometimes an ointment.

clue.text: A substantial amount to digest in principal series of lectures?

parts.note: principal means chief or main
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: A lecture series in which the chief subject is heavy going to take in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digest' suggests absorbing ideas from the lectures, but the definition is about eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The main course is the largest and most filling dish of a meal, the bulk of the food eaten.

clue.text: Man on board dismisses Latin class

indicators.note: dismisses means sends away, so the Latin letter is removed

parts.note: a castle is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A passenger aboard ship drops his Latin lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests someone on a ship; here it is a chess piece, as pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social group, especially in the Hindu system, so a rank or class of society.

clue.text: Impossible to avoid denying Spanish girl is qualified

indicators.note: denying means refusing a place to the girl's name, so it is removed from the longer word

parts.note: something impossible to avoid is inescapable
Ines is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: A fully trained professional, it seems, cannot help turning down a Spanish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A capable person has the ability and skill for a job, much as a qualified one is fit for it.

clue.text: One thousand English and Welsh dons long to see rise in vice

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the four letters are wrapped in the longing word like clothing

parts.note: to long for something is to crave it
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand English and Welsh university teachers yearn to witness wickedness on the increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university lecturers, but it is the verb: IMEW is put on inside CRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime wave is a sudden surge in the number of offences committed, an upturn in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Leaders of Transatlantic Trade & Investment Partnership rebuffed prime minister

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so those initials are read backwards
the leaders of the words are their opening letters, which make the trade deal's initials

explanation.surface: A premier turns down the proposed trade pact between the EU and the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: TTIP was the proposed EU–US trade deal of the 2010s.
explanation.definitionFit: Both William Pitt the Elder and his son Pitt the Younger served as British prime minister.

clue.text: Auntie is supposedly wrong to conceal weapon

indicators.note: to conceal says the wrong word hides the weapon inside it

parts.note: something wrong is bad
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: An elderly aunt, it is claimed, is wrong to hide a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC, which must by its charter be impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is obliged to give fair, even-handed coverage, so in theory its reporting is neutral.

clue.text: Tough old deputy

parts.note: ex means former or old
a deputy is acting in place of someone

explanation.surface: A former second-in-command is a hard nut.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting task or boss makes heavy demands, so is hard and tough to satisfy.

clue.text: Dissatisfaction seen in Nubia at regular intervals

indicators.note: at regular intervals says take every other letter of the words seen in Nubia, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A traveller notices discontent among the people of Nubia, the ancient land along the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a weary boredom and listlessness, a kind of dissatisfaction with everything around one.

clue.text: Wrong type of steering device, some say, could produce a spark

indicators.note: some say tells us the result is spoken, and a word that sounds like it is entered

parts.note: a wrong or moral offence is a sin; a tiller is the bar used to steer a boat

explanation.surface: Fitting the wrong kind of steering gear, people warn, could set off a spark.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, SIN plus TILLER gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or flicker of something; the word is Latin for a spark.

clue.text: Hawk, cock and hen in church yard

parts.note: dick is a slang word for a cock

indicators.note: in says the hen is placed inside the church's letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
hen is taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird of prey, a rooster and a hen all turn up in a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' is a bird alongside the cock and hen, but here it means a political hawk: Dick Cheney, US Vice President under George W Bush and a leading advocate of the Iraq war.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a hawk favours military force, and the former US Vice President was a famous example.

clue.text: One group of workers not on time

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the word on from the workers' group

parts.note: a trade union is a group of workers
on is taken as written

explanation.surface: A single body of employees refuses to keep to the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing counted as one whole, so it can stand for the number one.

clue.text: Institute of Reading organised financial assistance

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A research institute based in Reading arranges a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading here is the English town, not the act of reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign aid is money or support a country gives to help another, a form of financial assistance.

clue.text: New sort of mortal, curiously under wraps

indicators.note: wraps says the jumbled under goes round the jumbled mortal like a cover
curiously says the letters of under are jumbled in an odd way
sort of tells us the letters of mortal are given a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Some odd new kind of human being is being kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under wraps' looks like the idiom for secret, but it splits: 'curiously' jumbles under, 'sort of' jumbles mortal, and 'wraps' puts the second jumble just after the first one's opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ultramodern is extremely up to date, the very latest style, so it is new.

clue.text: Saint Itha converted some 16s

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint called Itha brought a few people over to her faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is ISLANDER: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahitians live on Tahiti, an island, so they are examples of island dwellers.

clue.text: Maybe Corfiot and I throw dirt

parts.note: to throw dirt at someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: A Greek from Corfu and I fling mud at each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corfiot lives on Corfu, a Greek island, so is one example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Antique keyboard in immaculate condition

definitions.meaning: an old small harpsichord-like instrument popular in Tudor England
pure and untouched, as a maiden is

explanation.surface: An old keyboard instrument that has been kept in perfect shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an early plucked keyboard instrument and the state of being a virgin, untouched and pure.

clue.text: Son's prudent to accept visit round school — it's full of holes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: to accept says the prudent word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a prudent person is wise

indicators.note: round says the visiting word goes round the school's letters

parts.note: to visit a person is to see them

explanation.surface: A boy is sensible enough to agree to a tour of his school, whose record is full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's full of holes' reads like a comment on the school, but it defines the answer. The nested piece sits after the first two letters of the prudent word.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental-style Swiss cheese is known for the large holes formed by gas bubbles as it ripens.

clue.text: Gill usually gives head

definitions.meaning: a small measure of drink, normally a quarter pint
slang for a person's head or brain

explanation.surface: A man called Gill normally offers a nod of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a small cup or measure of drink, often a gill, and informally a person's head.

clue.text: It's unpleasant lacking funds with financial liabilities

parts.note: OD is the abbreviation for overdrawn, a bank account lacking funds
IOUs are written promises to pay, debts owed

explanation.surface: Having no money and lots of debts is a nasty position to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful or repugnant, extremely disagreeable to deal with.

clue.text: A constellation in the past? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the past word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: something that happened in the past happened ago, as in long ago

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a star group belonged to former times, and gets told that's roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Argo Navis, the ship of Jason, was a large constellation of the southern sky, since split into smaller ones.

clue.text: Keep provoking Hardy and Nelson?

parts.note: hardy means tough or strong
a nelson is a wrestling hold, the arm locked behind an opponent's neck

explanation.surface: Captain Hardy and Admiral Nelson keep on annoying, as in the famous 'Kiss me, Hardy' scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy and Nelson look like the pair at Trafalgar (or the comedians Laurel and Hardy), but they are an adjective and a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the main tower of a castle, the fortified part used as a final place of defence.

clue.text: Junior member of parliament stuck in Glasgow letterbox

indicators.note: stuck in says the answer is wedged inside the words, running across their boundary

explanation.surface: A young MP's note is jammed in a postbox in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so a baby owl is a junior member of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a junior member of a parliament, the collective noun for a group of owls.

clue.text: Needled by 28 after swapping sides

indicators.note: after swapping sides says the word's two ends change places, as north and south swap on a compass

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, reports, means the same as news

explanation.surface: Annoyed by a news report once the parties changed allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: The synonym of 28 is NEWS; its two sides, N and S, change places.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled here means stitched with a needle, worked with thread, which is what sewn describes.

clue.text: Chad Allen trips in ballroom

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so the letters of the name fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Chad Allen loses his footing on the ballroom floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance hall is a large public room for dancing, much the same as a ballroom.

clue.text: Some scallywag group's belligerent behaviour

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gang of young rascals causes a spot of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation, meaning aggressive trouble-making or hostility.

clue.text: Advanced research all round is slackening

indicators.note: all round says the research letters go round the lent piece

parts.note: RES is the abbreviation for research
to advance money is to lend it, so advanced means lent

explanation.surface: A cutting-edge study across every field is losing momentum.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to ease off or soften, so something that relents is slackening.

clue.text: Container full of papers and grammar school reports

indicators.note: full of says the container has the papers inside it

parts.note: a tin is a container
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A box stuffed with documents and school reports is found.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old word for news, the reports that reach someone about events.
